structure: Part 11 read, in full and at commit c2078fb: the four DR2.1 views review-notification.html (104 lines), declaration.html (96), notification-submitted.html (86) and delete-notification.html (25); the five DR2.1 partials review-page-header.html (47), review-sections.html (54), review-summary-card.html (149), review-summary-row.html (32) and delete-confirmation.html (31); and app/routes.js lines 5146-6477 (review value formatting, the review view model and its error, read-only and cleared variants, the DR2 commodity, goods weight and temperature and document cards, the DR2 presentation and the status-to-variant map), 6562-6700 (dashboard notification metadata, the action-required warning, the review page header), 6904-7206 (review page options, renderReviewNotificationPage, the delete summary rows), 7279-7333 (delete view and render), 7419-7551 (declaration date, validateDeclaration, certificate messages, conditional submission items, renderDeclarationPage, renderNotificationSubmittedPage) and 13857-13992 (GET and POST /review-notification, GET and POST /notifications/delete, GET and POST /declaration, GET /notification-submitted). Helper definitions the slice calls were looked up where needed (hasJourneyUpdates and omitsContactAddressQuestion near line 320, requiresAnimalIdentifiersForSubmit at 2120, getIdentificationSpeciesLabel at 2224, toTitleCaseLabel at 830, the dashboard href builders and deleteNotification at 8250-8370, the GERMINAL_QUANTITY_LABEL and TEMPLATE_BLANK_ADDRESS_TEXT constants, and version-mount.js 255-294 for path prefixing). It covers four pages. The review page has three entry routes (journey, by submitted id, by reference) and five variants (journey, draft, submitted, submission-complete, action-required); outside the journey it shows a header with the reference, a status tag, an Actions menu (Amend, Make template, Copy as new, Delete), an action-required warning and a date, then an Import reference numbers section. Its body is five or six numbered sections of summary cards (About the consignment; Description of the goods; Transport and arrival; Uploaded documents, left out for a template; Addresses), with card errors, an error summary, the missing-field display and Change links, then the buttons per variant. The declaration page has three statements, one checkbox, its error and the submit that records the declaration and outstanding items. The notification-submitted page has the confirmation panel, the outstanding items, transport, view-or-amend and help sections. The delete page has its summary rows, the confirmation copy, Yes, delete and No, cancel, and the delete POST with its success message. Since the earlier extract the header buttons became an Actions menu, the contact address section and the Additional details card are no longer rendered, the addresses section and card were renamed, a goods weight and temperature card was added, species labels now lead with the common name, and germinal rows say Quantity; those claims carry new ids.

When the review page is opened with a submitted id that matches no submitted notification, the user is redirected to the dashboard.

When the review page is opened with no submitted id and no reference, it shows the in-progress notification from the session in the 'journey' variant: editable, with change links, no page header, and a Back link to the notification hub.

claims.statement: A notification's status text maps to a review variant: 'submitted' to submitted; 'submission complete', 'complete' or 'completed' to submission-complete; 'submitted action required' or 'action required' to action-required; anything else, including draft, new and in progress, to draft. The match ignores case and surrounding spaces.

Looked up by reference, a submitted notification's status is 'Submitted action required' when it has conditional submission items and 'Submitted' when it has none, and its date is the date it was submitted.

claims.statement: Looked up by reference, a saved draft notification shows its own status text, or 'Draft' when it has none, always in the draft variant, dated by when it was created.

A reference that is neither a submitted nor a saved draft notification is looked up in the dashboard's static example notifications, which take their variant from their own reviewVariant or their status text.

Every path the review, declaration, submitted and delete handlers redirect to or link to is served under /design-release-2.1, because the version mount prefixes redirects and rendered links with the release's base path.
claims.note: mechanism: the version mount rewrites root paths such as '/declaration' to the release's base path, so the handlers in this slice write root paths.

claims.statement: The delete-notification page is at GET /notifications/delete and needs a submitted id or a reference in the query; without one, or outside a design-release session, it redirects to the dashboard.
When the reference is the notification currently being worked on and is not yet saved anywhere, the delete page still opens, with its Back link and 'No, cancel' going to the review page.
When the submitted id or reference matches no notification and is not the one being worked on, the delete page redirects to the dashboard.
For a saved notification, the delete page's Back link and 'No, cancel' go back to that notification's review page from the dashboard.
The delete-notification page shows the Alpha phase banner and a 'Back' link.
The delete-notification page heading is 'Delete this notification?'.
The delete-notification page shows a summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin'.

The delete page's Commodity row lists each commodity's common name with its species' Latin names in brackets, each word title-cased, comma-separated (for example 'Cattle (Bison Bison, Bos Taurus)'); for 'other live mammals' each species' common name is used.
claims.note: The earlier extract's example kept the Latin names in sentence case; toTitleCaseLabel capitalises every word.

claims.statement: The delete page's Number row shows the total number of packages for a germinal-products-only notification, and otherwise the total number of animals.
The delete page's Origin row shows the country of origin.
A delete page summary row with no value from the notification falls back to the dashboard's listing for it, and shows 'Not applicable' when that is empty too.
Below the summary the delete page reads 'Confirm that you want to delete this notification.' and 'This action cannot be undone.'
The delete page has a red 'Yes, delete' button that posts to /notifications/delete with the same submitted id or reference.
Beside 'Yes, delete' the delete page has a 'No, cancel' link going to the same place as the Back link.
Confirming the delete removes the notification identified by the submitted id or reference.
Deleting by reference also records the reference as deleted, so a dashboard example notification with that reference stops showing.
claims.note: mechanism: keeps a list of deleted references in the session; that the dashboard hides them is read from the list's name, not from code in this slice.

claims.statement: Deleting the notification currently being worked on also clears the in-progress journey from the session.
After a delete, the user is returned to the dashboard with the success message '<reference> has been deleted.', or 'Notification has been deleted.' when the reference is not known.
claims.quote:
? `${notificationReference} has been deleted.`
    : 'Notification has been deleted.'

claims.statement: The delete POST does not check that the notification exists or that the session is a design-release session before deleting and showing the success message.
claims.note: The handler ignores reviewOptions.redirectTo and has no session check, unlike the GET.

claims.statement: The source says nothing about deleting a notification that has already been submitted beyond the same confirmation: no rule limits delete to drafts, and the review header's Actions menu offers Delete for every status.
The 'Copy' buttons in the Import reference numbers section carry the text to copy, but the slice does not show what the user sees after copying (no confirmation message).
claims.note: Looked in the review view and its partials; the copy script is not in this part's read list.
